summary: Clarify why low-volume healthcheck/background probes are triggering tenant 429s for interactive requests
description:
Issue summary:
SoraAnalytics reports intermittent 429s for interactive chat endpoints during their nightly background telemetry sweep (low-volume healthcheck + probe jobs). The probes are light (single small request every 10s per host) but when the telemetry sweep runs across hundreds of workers it appears to push the tenant over a short-window burst and interactive chat calls receive 429s.

Impact:
- ~15% of interactive requests from SoraAnalytics in prod-us-west returning 429s during their nightly sweep window (23:30–00:15 PST).
- Customer-facing application shows degraded UX (stalling and retries).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool, prod-us-west, tenant id: t-sora-019 (provided on secure channel).
- Traffic mix: 70% interactive chat, 20% small background probes, 10% bulk embeddings (off-peak).

Observed behavior:
1) Between 23:30 and 00:15 the console shows tenant token bucket near 100% and short bursts of 429s correlate with telemetry sweep start.
2) Console quota readout refreshes to new credits but 429s continue for ~2–3 minutes after refill.
3) Throttle headers in responses show X-RateLimit-Remaining near 0 and Retry-After sometimes 3–7 seconds.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Deploy 150 small probe workers scheduled to run a lightweight status ping every 10s (each ping ~20 tokens).
2) Start probes simultaneously (they run a coordinated sweep).
3) Trigger an interactive chat request to the same tenant during the sweep.
4) Observe 429 or increased latency and retry cycles.

Logs / traces:
- Provided trace ids in secure attachment: trace-prod-usw-20260301-01z (corresponding to 23:34 PST spike).
- Console shot shows token bucket drop and then CLI credit refresh at 23:36:10 but 429 spikes until 23:38:30.

Temporary mitigation requested:
- Guidance on configuration best-practices to keep background probes from eating interactive burst credits.
- If possible, short-term recommendation we can apply to tenant-level config in Dedicated to prevent immediate customer impact.

Notes about what customer already tried:
- Staggering probe start times to a 60s jitter reduced peak but did not eliminate 429s.
- They attempted to reduce probe frequency from 10s to 30s and saw lower 429s but still persistent.
comments: Support (2026-03-01): Thanks for the detailed reproduction steps and traces — we've escalated to SRE for quota accounting review. Can you confirm how many distinct host IPs the probes originate from?
Customer (2026-03-01): Probes originate from ~120 ephemeral hosts (k8s job), NATed behind a small pool of 10 egress IPs. We also sent a HAR with throttle headers attached.

SRE (2026-03-02): Hypothesis: healthchecks/probes are being charged to the same tenant burst pool and the simultaneous start creates a microburst that exhausts the short-window refill. We'll look at refill timing and edge vs origin accounting.

Support (2026-03-02): Temporary action: Recommend enabling a split-burst pool (if available) for background jobs or configuring probe clients to add an explicit header to mark probe traffic for a lower-priority class. Customer asked how to do this on their side and whether Redwood can set a tenant-level exemption.
Customer (2026-03-03): Can you confirm whether enabling 'longpoll-exemption' or allocating an isolated burst lane for their probes will require a Dedicated config change or code change on their side?
investigation_notes: 03-02-2026: Downloaded trace-prod-usw-20260301-01z. Observed ~120 concurrent connections within 30s window, each ~20 tokens; aggregate consumed ~2400 tokens in <60s. Tenant short-window burst budget was set to 2000 tokens -> exhausted. Refill aligned to :00 and :30 seconds (window length 30s).

03-02-2026: Edge counting shows preflight and healthcheck pings counted on edge in addition to origin accounting due to proxy keepalive reuse; possible double-counting for HTTP/2 multiplexed connections. Need to verify per-connection vs per-request accounting in proxy config.
03-03-2026: Confirmed console shows credit refill but request queueing/backpressure results in delayed clearance; clients retry amplifies token consumption in the following window.

Hypothesis: Two contributing factors - (1) coordinated simultaneous probe start causing a true microburst that overwhelms short-window refill, (2) proxy/keepalive behavior causing additional token accounting (duplicate counts) for multiplexed probe hosts.
resolution: In progress - proposed multi-pronged fix: (A) Recommend customer stagger probe schedule with randomized jitter across a longer window (recommended: start jitter 0-300s instead of synchronous start); (B) For Dedicated tenants, SRE can enable an isolated 'background' burst lane to keep low-value probes from drawing interactive credits — this requires a config flag flip on the tenant (scheduled); (C) Patch to edge accounting to avoid double-counting HTTP/2 multiplexed preflights (PR referenced). Short-term: we enabled a temporary tenant-level priority-split for t-sora-019 and observed 80% reduction in interactive 429s during a controlled probe run. Follow-ups: rollout PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/432, run audit for proxy accounting, and publish runbook for customers running large coordinated background sweeps.
